inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: Title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion name the same contribution or contributions, and every reported study has a Methods description outside Results.
inherited_criterion.letter_text: Title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion name the same contribution or contributions, and every reported study has a Methods description outside Results.

operationalization.fully_addressed: [routed: EIC / Journal-Fit Reviewer, card #1] Either Round-1 route is admissible. (a) Single-study route: the title, abstract, section 1 contribution list and section 11 conclusion all name the calibration-coverage study as the contribution; the five accuracy sweeps (Round-1 sections 7.9-7.13) are not named as a contribution on any of those four surfaces (at most a pointer to an appendix or separate report); any sweep material kept in the document has its own methods description outside Results. (b) Two-question route: section 1 states two research questions; title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion each name the same two contributions; the sweep program and the calibration study each have a methods description outside the Results section. Check: list the contribution(s) named on each of the four surfaces (the sets must be identical) and, for every study whose results are reported, locate its methods description in a non-Results section.
operationalization.partially_addressed: The four surfaces agree but the sweep methods still appear only inside Results; or methods were moved out of Results but one surface names a different contribution set (e.g., title calibration-only while abstract and conclusion still carry both studies, or the abstract still closes on the sweep result under route (a)); or two research questions are stated in section 1 without matching Methods structure.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The contribution sets named across title, abstract, contribution list and conclusion diverge more than in the original (e.g., an additional study or contribution named on some surfaces only); or a reported study's methods that sat outside Results now sit inside Results; or a new study is reported without its own methods description.

items.expected_change_surface: Title; Abstract; section 1 (research question, contribution list); sections 7.9-7.13 (sweep rounds); section 8 Discussion; section 11 Conclusion; a possible new Methods subsection or appendix (roadmap cost scope: Title, Abstract, section 1, sections 7.9-7.13, section 8, section 11).

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: §2.4 characterizes the named calibration-data literature, and the §1 and §8.1 novelty statement names the time-series-specific mechanism instead of "nominal sample count said nothing".
inherited_criterion.letter_text: §2.4 characterizes the named calibration-data literature, and the §1 and §8.1 novelty statement names the time-series-specific mechanism instead of "nominal sample count said nothing".

operationalization.fully_addressed: [routed: EIC / Journal-Fit Reviewer, card #1] Section 2.4 (or an equivalent Related Work location) contains a calibration-data-selection paragraph that characterizes, not merely cites, what the named works report about calibration-data choice: Williams and Aletras 2024; Yu, Yang and Shi 2021; Cai et al. 2020 (ZeroQ); Krishnamoorthi 2018; Nagel et al. 2021; Wu et al. 2020 (a substantively equivalent set covering calibration-data choice as a studied lever, calibration-data statistics/representativeness, and range setting from calibration data is admissible), with matching reference-list entries. AND the novelty statement in section 1 and in section 8.1 is stated around the time-series-specific mechanism (overlapping, time-ordered windows concentrating a nominal calibration set on one or two participants, with its class-asymmetric clipping consequence), and neither place presents 'nominal sample count said nothing' (or a paraphrase making nominal count the novel finding) as the novelty. Consistent with the Requirement: the result is framed as confirmation and measurement of a known lever.
operationalization.partially_addressed: The named literature is cited only as a list without characterization, or only a subset is engaged with no equivalent coverage; or section 2.4 is fixed but section 1 or section 8.1 still states the novelty as 'nominal sample count said nothing'; or the novelty is restated in only one of section 1 / section 8.1.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: The novelty claim is broadened (e.g., calibration-data selection itself claimed as a new lever), the named works are characterized inaccurately in a way that inflates novelty, or the time-series-specific mechanism disappears from the novelty statement.

items.expected_change_surface: Section 2.4 Related Work; section 1 novelty statement and contribution list; section 8.1; reference list.

inherited_criterion.roadmap_text: No sentence credits the flatten head or the cosine schedule with an improvement unless a multi-seed RT-CGM comparison is reported, and every citation of the +0.20-point gain states the seed spread.
inherited_criterion.letter_text: No sentence credits the flatten head or the cosine schedule with an improvement unless a multi-seed RT-CGM comparison is reported, and every citation of the +0.20-point gain states the seed spread.

operationalization.fully_addressed: [routed: EIC / Journal-Fit Reviewer, card #1] Either Round-1 route is admissible. (b) Artifact-level route: the contribution list, abstract and conclusion, and every other sentence that summarizes round five, describe it as a pre-registered ship decision between the specific seed-4 candidate artifact and the champion artifact (e.g., 'the seed-4 flatten-head artifact passed the pre-registered gates'); no sentence credits the flatten head, a position-preserving head, or the cosine schedule with an improvement; and every occurrence of the +0.20-point gain states the 1.1-point five-seed spread in the same or adjacent sentence. (a) Multi-seed route: a multi-seed RT-CGM comparison of the candidate and champion recipes is reported (Requirement: all five seeds of each recipe, labelled descriptive because the confirmatory read is spent, with seed-and-participant uncertainty such as a two-stage bootstrap or a mixed model; an equivalent seed-aware uncertainty is admissible), any remaining head or schedule credit is no stronger than that comparison shows, and every occurrence of the +0.20-point gain still states the seed spread. Check: enumerate every '+0.20' / '0.20 points' occurrence and every sentence naming the head or schedule as a source of improvement.
operationalization.partially_addressed: Artifact-level wording is adopted on some summary surfaces but at least one sentence (e.g., contribution list 'confirmed' or conclusion 'promoted') still credits the head or the schedule; or the seed spread accompanies the +0.20 gain in some occurrences but not all; or a multi-seed analysis is reported only on validation/held-out data rather than RT-CGM, or without seed-level variation shown, while head or schedule credit is retained.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: A new design-level credit to the head or the schedule appears without multi-seed RT-CGM evidence; a multi-seed RT-CGM analysis is presented as confirmatory or used to re-certify the design; the seed spread is removed from a place it appeared; or multi-seed results inside seed noise are presented as supporting the head.

operationalization.fully_addressed: [routed: EIC / Journal-Fit Reviewer, card #1] Every passage that Round 1 found calling the sequential arm the toolchain default (six passages: Abstract, section 1, section 5.2, section 7.8, section 8.1, section 11) either uses a neutral description (e.g., 'contiguous first-N, dataset-order selection') or, if the default label is kept, cites a toolchain source naming the toolchain, version and example code that feeds calibration data in stored order; no other passage introduces the label without such a source. AND section 8.1 quotes the cited RepresentativeDataset guidance's instruction that the calibration subset be randomly chosen, in no particular order (quotation with citation). operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: Additional passages describe the sequential arm as a default or common practice without a source; the guidance is misquoted; or a cited source is added that does not show stored-order feeding (miscitation).

AND section 7.7 reports each designated contrast with its point estimate and interval (Round-1 record: dubosson temporal about +2.0 [-0.0, +3.1] points, lower bound -0.0000338; hall held-out about +1.3 [-0.1, +3.3] points) and states the outcome of the hall premise (assumed ceiling near 240 mg/dL; realized sequential ceiling 165 mg/dL, so the premise was contradicted). operationalization.partially_addressed: Confirmation wording is removed from some of the four Round-1 locations but kept, or replaced by an equivalent confirmation claim, in at least one; or section 7.7 reports both designated intervals but not the hall premise outcome; or reports the premise outcome but omits one designated interval.
operationalization.made_worse_discriminator: New confirmation language is added (e.g., a post-hoc decision rule or margin introduced to declare a prediction held); a designated interval is misreported (e.g., a lower bound rounded to a positive value); the hall premise failure is concealed; or hall's temporal +4.3 is presented as confirming the hall prediction.

The R3 Requirement and EIC-W2 (the stated basis of the EIC's D6 block, trigger 'the closest prior on-device, quantized or health time-series work is missing') also ask for a paragraph on quantized on-device health and wearable time-series classifiers, and the R2 Acceptance criterion covers only the calibration-data literature, so no Round-1 acceptance criterion carries this element.

new_standards.standard_text: Section 7.7 should label the second-cohort interpretation exploratory and report hall's temporal component (+4.3 [+1.1, +7.3] points) beside the inconclusive designated hall contrast.
new_standards.why_not_in_round1: Both elements are in the R6 Requirement and in the letter's D2 resolution (R1's remedy adopted; EIC's added hall-temporal sentence kept), but the R6 Acceptance criterion requires only the removal of 'held' and 'reproduced' claims, the designated contrasts with intervals, and the hall premise outcome.

new_standards.standard_text: Any remaining label-robustness sentence should cite a CGM sensor-error model (e.g., Facchinetti et al. 2014), and section 7.12 should state that the labels are defined on the sensor trace (the future CGM-reported rate, not the blood-glucose rate).
